answer: An agent economy blunts Sybil attacks by bonding every identity in an escrowed stake plus a non-refundable fee. Each new agent locks collateral on-chain, so a farm of a thousand voices costs a thousand times the single deposit, frozen for the whole epoch. Slashing burns the lock permanently, so nothing is recycled after a vote, and loose shale cannot pile into free identities. Reputation decays slowly and a fresh account cannot inherit it, so raw marble must be quarried block by block. The delta between honest reward and attack cost stays steep: each added voice costs the same as the first.
